q: A 7m x 12m room gets flooring finish: two-thirds of the area in 60x60 ceramic tile, the rest in wood. With a 5% allowance for spacing and wastage, how many tiles are needed?
n: The tiled portion covers 2/3 of the 84 sqm room (a 7m x 8m section = 56 sqm). At 0.6m x 0.6m per tile, that's 12 tiles across the 7m width and 14 tiles along the 8m length = 168 pieces; rounding up at the cut edges already absorbs the 5% allowance.

q: What metal alloy consists of copper and tin?
n: Bronze is a copper-tin alloy by definition; brass is copper-zinc, Muntz metal is a copper-zinc variant, and terne is a lead-tin coating over steel.

q: What is the minimum ultimate strength of structural-grade steel (PNS-49 Gr. 230) bars?
n: PNS 49 Grade 230 (equivalent to ASTM A615 Grade 33) has a minimum ultimate/tensile strength of about 56,000 psi.

q: What is it called when the last member of a building frame is placed?
n: "Topping-out" marks the placement of the final, highest structural member of a building frame, traditionally celebrated with a topping-out ceremony.

q: Which process revolutionized flat glass production?
n: The float glass process, developed by Pilkington in the 1950s, replaced older cylinder/plate methods and became the standard for producing flat glass economically.

q: What do you call a twisting force?
n: Torsion is the internal twisting force or moment acting about a member's longitudinal axis.

q: What is the Filipino vernacular term for a horizontal stud?
n: "Pabalagbag" is the vernacular term for the horizontal stud, paired conceptually with "pilarete" for the vertical stud.

q: Which is the largest rebar manufacturer in the Philippines?
n: SteelAsia Manufacturing Corporation is widely recognized as the largest reinforcing-steel-bar manufacturer in the Philippines.

q: Which roofing metal is specified by weight in pounds?
n: Sheet lead is traditionally specified by weight per square foot (e.g., "4 lb." lead), a holdover from lead flashing and roofing trade practice.

q: Which of these is NOT used as a supplementary cementitious material (SCM) in concrete?
n: Fly ash, silica fume, and slag cement are all standard, ASTM-recognized SCMs used to partially replace portland cement; diatomaceous earth isn't classified as an SCM.

q: What term describes resistance to high temperatures?
n: "Refractory" describes a material's resistance to decomposition or deformation under high heat, as used for kiln linings and fireproofing.

q: What is the trim called that sits at wainscot height, usually level with a window sill?
n: A chair rail is a horizontal trim band at wainscot/sill height, traditionally meant to protect the wall from chair backs.

q: Thermal mass depends on a material's heat capacity and density together. At an equal 100mm thickness, which of these generates the highest thermal mass?
n: Thermal mass per unit thickness follows volumetric heat capacity (density x specific heat). Water's value exceeds steel, concrete, and wood, making it the best thermal-mass generator at equal thickness.

q: What do you call a piece of lumber with a dimension under 2 inches?
n: By standard lumber-grading convention, "boards" are pieces under 2 inches nominal thickness; "dimension lumber" runs 2-5 inches, and "timbers" are 5 inches or more.

q: Which metal-roof manufacturer does NOT offer curved roofs in its product line?
n: ColorSteel, Metalink, and Puyat all explicitly offer curved-roof product lines; Jacinto Color Steel's roofing lineup does not include a curved-roof option.

q: Light-gauge furring shapes separate a metal roof from its substrate for several reasons. Which is NOT one of those reasons?
o: To give a location to attach the roof panel clip.
To adjust for movement from thermal expansion.
To provide support for the roof panels.
n: Furring shapes space, ventilate, insulate, and provide a fastening surface for the roof — the panels' actual structural support comes from the purlins or deck underneath, not the spacer itself.

q: What is the ASTM designation for ready-mix concrete?
n: ASTM C94 is the Standard Specification for Ready-Mixed Concrete.

q: What is a column feature that projects from a building's corner called?
n: A "canton" is a pilaster-like decorative feature projecting at a building's corner (quoin), distinct from an engaged column or pilaster set on a flat wall face.

q: What is the Filipino vernacular term for a joist?
n: "Suleras" (or "soleras") is the standard vernacular term for a floor joist; "biga" means beam, "kostilyahe" means ceiling joist, and "guililan" means girder.

q: Which cement manufacturer has plants across Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao?
n: Republic Cement operates plants across all three major island groups, giving it the widest geographic manufacturing footprint among local producers.

q: Which of these roofing metals is NOT specified by gauge number?
n: Steel, stainless steel, and zinc roofing stock are conventionally called out by gauge number; aluminum is specified by decimal inch thickness instead.

q: What is the minimum ultimate strength of intermediate-grade steel (PNS-49 Gr. 280) bars?
n: PNS 49 Grade 280 (ASTM Grade 40 equivalent) carries a minimum ultimate/tensile strength of 60,000 psi.

q: Which of these is NOT a bituminous material?
n: Asphalt, pitch, and tar are all bituminous, hydrocarbon-based materials; bentonite is a clay used for waterproofing and drilling mud, with no bitumen content.

q: All but one of these are structural steel members with open sections. Which is the exception?
n: HP (bearing pile), OWSJ (open web steel joist), and WT (structural tee) are open-section shapes; HSS (hollow structural section) is a closed, tubular section.

q: Making an outlet opening (e.g., a window) bigger than the inlet increases indoor airflow rate. What is this effect called?
n: Sizing the outlet larger than the inlet accelerates indoor air velocity — a constriction-based acceleration effect classified as the Venturi effect, distinct from the buoyancy-driven stack/chimney effect.

q: What is the Filipino vernacular term for a vertical stud?
n: "Pilarete" denotes the vertical stud in Philippine construction vernacular, distinct from "pabalagbag" (horizontal stud) and "tabike" (external siding).

q: Which company produces only light-gauge steel products?
n: JEA Steel Industries manufactures exclusively light-gauge steel profiles (drywall studs/tracks, ceiling systems, purlins); the others also produce rebar and/or structural steel.

q: Which roofing metal is specified only by thickness in inches, not by gauge?
n: Unlike steel, which uses gauge numbers, aluminum roofing/flashing stock is conventionally called out by decimal thickness in inches (e.g., .032", .040").

q: What is the minimum specified compressive strength for ultra-high performance concrete?
n: Ultra-high performance concrete (UHPC) is generally defined with a minimum specified compressive strength around 17,000 psi (117 MPa) or greater.

q: What is the main ingredient of glass?
n: Silica sand is the principal raw material of glass by mass (roughly 70%), with soda ash and limestone/dolomite added as fluxing and stabilizing agents.

q: What do you call a single-slope roof, also known as a shed, pent, or lean-to roof?
n: "Skillion roof" is the architectural term for a single-sloping roof, synonymous with shed, pent, and lean-to forms.

q: One third of an 84 sqm room floor (28 sqm) is finished in wood flooring using KD 1x8x4 dimension lumber. How many pieces are needed, with no allowance?
n: The wood-floored third is 28 sqm. At the actual dressed width of a nominal 1x8 (7-1/4" = 0.184 m) over a 4-ft (1.219 m) length, each piece covers about 0.2245 sqm; 28 / 0.2245 ≈ 124.7, rounded up to 125 pieces.

q: What alloy consists essentially of copper and zinc?
n: Brass is the standard term for a copper-zinc alloy. (Muntz metal is technically a specific brass, roughly 60% copper/40% zinc, but "brass" is the general answer.)

q: Which brand belongs to Puyat Steel's product line?
n: "APO" (and APO Galfan) is the long-standing flagship roofing brand of Puyat Steel Corporation, manufacturer since 1956.

q: What is the term for removing formwork from cured concrete?
n: "Stripping" (or "form stripping") is the standard term for removing formwork once concrete has cured sufficiently.

q: What is the ASTM designation for load-bearing CMU?
n: ASTM C90 is the Standard Specification for Loadbearing Concrete Masonry Units; C33 covers concrete aggregates, C94 ready-mixed concrete, and C150 Portland cement.

q: What is the simplest space-frame unit, having only 6 structural members?
n: A tetrahedron, the simplest 3D polyhedral truss unit, has exactly 6 edges and 4 triangular faces, making it the basic building block of space-frame structures.

q: What is the Filipino vernacular term for a rabbet?
n: "Vaciada" (literally "hollowed-out") is the vernacular term for a rabbet, a recessed groove cut along an edge; "palitada" refers to plastering and "zocalo" to a base or skirting.

q: Which is the largest local cement manufacturer in the Philippines?
n: Holcim Philippines has long been regarded as the country's largest cement producer by market share.

q: Which roofing metal is specified by weight in ounces?
n: Copper sheet is specified by weight in ounces per square foot (e.g., 16 oz. or 20 oz. copper), the traditional copper roofing standard.

q: What is the minimum yield strength of intermediate-grade steel (PNS-49 Gr. 280) bars?
n: PNS 49 Grade 280 (equivalent to ASTM A615 Grade 40) has a minimum yield strength of 40,000 psi (280 MPa).

q: What do you call Portland cement concrete with less cement paste than a typical mix?
n: "Lean concrete" denotes a mix with reduced cement content relative to standard structural concrete, commonly used for sub-base and blinding layers.

q: All but one of these wall systems use EPS rigid board as a component. Which is the exception?
n: EIFS, ICF, and SIP systems commonly use EPS (expanded polystyrene) rigid board; GFRC (glass-fiber-reinforced concrete) is a cementitious cladding panel with no EPS.

q: Which flooring material shows the lowest thermal mass?
n: WPC (wood-plastic composite) planks have far lower density and volumetric heat capacity than ceramic tile, pebble washout, or clay Vigan tiles.

q: What do you call a piece of lumber whose smallest dimension is at least 5 inches?
n: "Timbers" are lumber with both cross-sectional dimensions of 5 inches or greater, distinguishing them from boards (under 2") and dimension lumber (2-5").

q: "Galvalume" is a product associated with which company?
n: Union Galvasteel Corporation (UGC) is the licensed Philippine manufacturer of Galvalume (55% aluminum-zinc) coated steel products.

q: In the furring-profile figure, which labeled shape lets you level out an irregular substrate by adjusting piece-by-piece?
n: The telescoping, overlapping profile (D) can slide to vary its height along its length, unlike the fixed-dimension hat and Z/C-channels (A, F, H).

q: What term describes concrete with compressive strength above 6,000 psi?
n: High-strength concrete is generally defined as exceeding 6,000 psi (41 MPa); "high-performance" and "ultra-high-performance" concrete describe broader or higher performance thresholds.

q: What is the lateral deflection of a structure called?
n: "Drift" is the standard term for the lateral displacement of a building or story under lateral loads such as wind or seismic forces.

q: Which vernacular term refers specifically to a ceiling joist?
n: "Kostilyahe" specifically denotes the ceiling joist, distinct from "suleras" (floor joist) and "guililan" (girder).
